page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7se.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.9 GHz. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The underlying x86_64 architecture supports AVX, AVX-512 (including VNNI), and cryptographic acceleration instructions like AES and SHA_NI.

Performance benchmarks indicate a discrepancy between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core execution, such as stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests, falls within the average tier, supported by the 2.9 GHz Intel Xeon processor. However, multi-core performance in stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark CPU tests is categorized as weak, reflecting the physical limitation of its 2-core, 4-thread topology. Memory bandwidth benchmarks, including uncached read and write operations, also register in the lower performance tier. Cryptographic operations and single-threaded decompression tasks perform at average levels, whereas database operations, Redis SET throughput, and static web serving are comparatively weak.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g7se.xlarge offers a balanced resource allocation for workloads that do not require high-throughput memory or intensive parallel processing. It is suitable for general-purpose applications, light web serving, text processing, and single-threaded utility tasks. The lack of local storage and modest network bandwidth make it less suitable for high-performance databases, large-scale ETL pipelines, or memory-intensive data science jobs.
